samples: This program downloads every customer from a cursor-paginated web API, following each page's "next" pointer until none remains, and then prints how many customers live in each country, largest group first. It needs network access to a single hard-coded API address and console output, and it stops with an HTTP or JSON error if a request or response parsing fails. It includes a test that replays recorded responses offline to check that all pages are collected, so you can verify it without hitting the live service, though you would need to change the address to use it with your own API.

This program downloads the full customer list from a cursor-paginated web API (at `api.example.com`) by requesting each page in turn and following the "next cursor" value until the API stops providing one, then prints how many customers are in each country, largest group first. It needs network access and console output, and it stops with an HTTP or JSON-parsing error if a request fails or a response isn't in the expected shape. It includes a test that replays recorded responses offline and checks that three customers are collected, so you can verify the paging logic without hitting the live service.

This program downloads every customer from a cursor-paginated web API at a fixed example address, following each page's "next" cursor until the API stops returning one, and then prints how many customers each country has, with the largest country first. It needs network access and console output, and it stops with an HTTP or JSON error if a request fails or a response can't be parsed. Its main function has the API address hardcoded, but the page-fetching function takes any base address, and a bundled test replays a recorded response offline and checks that three customers come back.

This program downloads every customer from a cursor-paginated web API, following each page's "next" cursor until the API stops returning one, and then prints how many customers live in each country, largest group first. It needs network access and console output, and it stops with an HTTP or JSON error if a request fails or a response can't be parsed. The endpoint is hardcoded in the main function, so you would need to change it to point at your own API. It includes a test that replays a recorded response and expects three customers.

This program downloads every customer from a cursor-paginated web API, requesting page after page until the API stops returning a "next page" marker, and gathers them into one list. It then prints how many customers there are in each country, with the largest country first. The program needs network access and console output. It fails if an HTTP request or JSON parse goes wrong, and it comes with a test that replays a recorded fixture and expects three customers.
